author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Midnight Deadline
challenge.description: The nightly data job is failing to finish before the store managers open the ordering app. #reliability_ruth# demands an automated validation layer to catch bad data instantly so the morning window is never missed again. #data_dave# insists on keeping the process manual for now, arguing that the infrastructure costs are too high and the current manual checks are sufficient to manage the risk.

output.content: I am open to automating the hand over from validation to versioning, but I will accept losing our current manual control only if the work rides on tooling we already license. If we use existing infrastructure, I can trade the two in the morning manual click for a fully automated step without any new licensing fees. I am prepared to give up the safety net of a human review at that specific junction, provided the cost remains zero. I will not spend new budget on this, but I am willing to accept the risk of an unattended transition if it is free.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states a willingness to give up manual control and human review safety nets in exchange for automation, provided it is achieved without new licensing fees.
